purpose: Provide a first-class invitation for people and institutions to bring Boundary First Labs a complicated, overloaded, brittle, opaque, exception-ridden, or consequence-bearing system without requiring them to first know which Lab method, product, service, or research program applies.
posture: This is a bounded problem-intake interface, not a claim that Boundary First Labs can solve every problem or possesses domain authority in every field. A successful intake may route to reconstruction, audit, build, validation, governance, partnership, referral, or stop.
title: Bring Us Your Difficult System

hero.headline: Bring us your difficult system.
hero.body: Overloaded, brittle, opaque, exception-ridden, or consequence-bearing is fine. You do not need to translate the problem into Boundary First vocabulary first. Start with what is happening, what keeps breaking, and what you cannot afford to lose.
hero.secondary: Before we prescribe a solution, let's make sure we are solving the right system.

coreInvitation.statement: Bring us your complicated problem. Bring us the overloaded system. Let's make it legible enough to repair.
coreInvitation.promise: Help reconstruct the system well enough to decide what kind of problem it is, what evidence matters, what Boundary First Labs can responsibly contribute, and what should happen next.
coreInvitation.nonPromise: Diagnosis does not guarantee repair, acceptance, domain authority, implementation, or a continuing engagement.

failurePatterns.label: Overloaded representation
symptoms: one object carries too many meanings
important distinctions survive only as insider convention
different teams use the same representation differently
local efficiency creates global confusion
failurePatterns.prompt: Too much reality has been compressed into one representation. What did it forget?

failurePatterns.label: Exception-built system
symptoms: happy path is clean but actual operation is dominated by workarounds
policy and implementation disagree
edge cases have become normal operation
hidden labor absorbs defects
failurePatterns.prompt: Show us the exceptions. They often reveal the real system.

failurePatterns.label: Responsibility gap
symptoms: authority can act but responsibility does not land
many teams own parts but nobody owns consequence
affected people cannot reach contest or repair
escalation ends in another handoff
failurePatterns.prompt: Who can act, who is affected, and who can actually repair the result?

failurePatterns.label: Brittle software / inherited system
symptoms: nobody wants to change it
local fixes break distant paths
business rules are spread across code, tickets, memory, and incidents
interfaces conceal state
failurePatterns.prompt: Before rewriting it, let's recover the object the software is trying to represent.

failurePatterns.label: Maintenance / lifecycle debt
symptoms: launch succeeded but ownership disappeared
deferred obligations sit outside success metrics
temporary human processes became permanent infrastructure
replacement or retirement has no owner
failurePatterns.prompt: What must continually be supplied for this capability to remain real?

failurePatterns.label: Evidence / knowledge overload
symptoms: information multiplies faster than conclusions can be trusted
provenance disappears in synthesis
contradictions are hard to recover
authoritative status is unclear
failurePatterns.prompt: The problem may not be information scarcity. It may be governed continuity.

failurePatterns.label: Cross-boundary failure
symptoms: components work locally but the whole fails at handoffs
meaning, state, authority, or responsibility changes at interfaces
the defect is always somebody else's part
failurePatterns.prompt: Let's inspect the crossing, not just the components on either side.

failurePatterns.label: Wicked / unstable problem
symptoms: defining the problem changes it
interventions create new actors or constraints
there is no clean single objective
solutions export consequence elsewhere
failurePatterns.prompt: Start with the present boundary, preserve uncertainty, act narrowly, observe consequence, and update the representation.

intakeQuestions: What seems to break when you change it?
Who owns repair if the change causes harm or failure?
What would a meaningfully better state look like?
What are we not allowed to assume?

routingClasses.label: Reconstruct
routingClasses.when: The main defect is that nobody has a trustworthy model of the system.

routingClasses.label: Audit
routingClasses.when: Authority, consequence, contestability, responsibility, or repair are central.

routingClasses.label: Build / Repair
routingClasses.when: The bounded representation is understood well enough to construct or repair an instrument or implementation.

routingClasses.label: Test / Validate
routingClasses.when: A claim, model, intervention, or representation needs a native witness.

routingClasses.label: Govern / Steward
routingClasses.when: Ownership, maintenance, authority, versioning, retirement, or transfer are the core problem.

routingClasses.label: Refer / Partner
routingClasses.when: The next responsible step requires domain authority, infrastructure, access, standing, or stewardship BFL should not reproduce alone.

routingClasses.label: Stop / Decline
routingClasses.when: The intervention exceeds authority, cannot be bounded responsibly, lacks evidence, requires false claims, or has no lawful competence/partnership path.

firstEngagement.principle: Do not jump from a messy story directly to a large implementation proposal.

capitalRelation.statement: Problem intake is the inverse input manifold to Capital: Capital asks what capacity should enter the Lab; Problem Input asks what difficult reality should enter the inquiry machinery.
capitalRelation.capitalEffect: Capital increases the Lab's capacity to receive and close more of these loops without lowering evidence, governance, or stewardship standards.

copyModules.globalCta: Have a difficult system? Bring it to the Lab.
copyModules.globalBody: Overloaded software, tangled workflows, unclear responsibility, hidden maintenance, evidence sprawl, brittle handoffs—start with the problem as it actually exists.
copyModules.voiceLine: Bring us the mess: the exceptions, the workarounds, the half-true diagram, the five owners, the spreadsheet everyone is afraid to touch.
copyModules.professionalLine: We reconstruct consequence-bearing systems before prescribing solutions: actors, artifacts, authority, state, invariants, interfaces, evidence, failure paths, and repair obligations.
copyModules.humanLine: You do not need to make the problem sound simple before you contact us. Complicated is the point.
copyModules.closing: If the problem crosses boundaries faster than your current tools can follow it, bring us the system. Let's find out what is actually happening.

claimBoundary: No claim of universal cross-domain expertise.
No legal, clinical, regulatory, financial, safety, or other professional authority unless independently established.
No implication that every intake becomes an engagement.
No implication of a large consulting team or unlimited current capacity.
No claim that a Boundary First diagnosis validates Boundary Theory.
